data.title: Materials Shares Rise as Metal Prices Tick Higher — Materials Roundup
data.description:
Producers of metals, grains and other raw materials rose as gold futures snapped a four-session losing streak as the U.S. dollar pulled back following four straight sessions of gains. Silver and copper also rose.

ArcelorMittal said it cannot safely restart operations at its Ukrainian subsidiary after missile attacks killed five people and injured 17 employees, and expects to record a $1 billion impairment. The Luxembourg-based steelmaker said Friday that four missile strikes at ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih over the past five weeks also caused extensive damage to production facilities. The most recent attack was on Monday. The expected noncash impairment charge mainly relates to damaged property, plant and equipment at the site in Kryvyi Rih, central Ukraine.

Largo shares were sharply lower Friday after the company priced its $5.7 million offering below recent trading prices. The Canadian miner on Friday said it would offer 10.2 million units at a price of 56 cents apiece.

data.title: Industrial Shares Among Top Gainers Amid Signs of Resilient Economy — Industrials Roundup
data.description:
A broad recovery in U.S. stock markets lifted shares in the industrial sector. Economic indicators have pointed to resilient growth despite elevated borrowing costs.

Demand for U.S. durable goods was unchanged in August, according to data published by the Commerce Department, beating forecasts of a small contraction. Total orders for durable goods decreased $0.1 billion in August to $338.6 billion, following a 0.9% July increase. Transportation equipment, down three of the last four months, drove the decrease, falling 0.6%. Excluding defense, new orders increased 0.1%.

Bloom Energy jumped Friday after a Wall Street firm reassured investors that the company won't be affected by Oracle's push to protect itself against potential delays on its massive data-center project. Oracle sent a force majeure notice Thursday to Stack Infrastructure, the developer of its Project Jupiter campus in New Mexico, Bloomberg reported.

Corecivic said its president and chief executive has resigned, citing health reasons. The private prison operator before the bell said Patrick Swindle, who is pursuing treatment for stage-four metastatic pancreatic cancer, would step down after less than a year at the helm. He has also resigned from the company's board.

Tesla will begin deliveries of its all-electric Semi truck to customers this week, after years of delays. The heavy-duty Semi was announced by Elon Musk in November 2017. At the time, the company had plans to kick off production a few years later. However, the company repeatedly pushed back the launch, preventing it from being able to serve the long-haul freight market on its original timeline.

data.title: Microsoft's stock has roared back to life, closing at its highest level of the year
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

Microsoft shares got off to a rough start this year, but investors have warmed to the company's AI narrative over the past few months

Shares of Microsoft just closed at their highest level of 2026.

Microsoft has positioned itself as a software company that isn't exclusively tied to any of the big artificial-intelligence model makers, and that's shaping up to be a key advantage, according to an analyst.

Shares of Microsoft (MSFT) have climbed well off their 2026 lows and closed up 3.66% on Friday, at $516.17 - clinching their highest close since November.

On Friday, the stock was also the best performer in the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, the index that tracks 30 major stocks meant to represent the U.S. economy.

Microsoft's stock has been gaining since the company posted earnings for its latest quarter, up 32% from the time of that report in late July.

See also: The old new thing: Cisco and retro tech are back and forming the AI buildout's backbone

D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria told MarketWatch that Microsoft is "finally getting credit again for how well it is positioned to benefit from the growth of AI."

Microsoft's stock was punished earlier this year, as AI fears loomed large over the software sector. Through July 28, the stock was down about 17% since the start of the year.

The company is "helping their customers manage the frontier models in a more efficient and effective way" than other companies, Luria said. He referred to how Microsoft's software can be a base from which to use different AI models and agents for different workflows - a software concept known as an "orchestration layer," which Microsoft has "wisely moved into," Luria explained. Frontier models are those deemed to be on the cutting edge of what AI has to offer.

Microsoft's approach allows companies to switch frontier models based on which one is best suited for different types of tasks.

Luria also expects growth of the company's core Azure cloud-computing platform to accelerate further. There's also room for the company to capitalize on the rise of AI assistants.

On Friday, Microsoft released a new version of Copilot, its AI-powered assistant that aims to help customers get more out of the company's software offerings. Luria said that the latest Microsoft introduction aims to "replicate Meta Muse's success for businesses," referring to Meta's new personal AI agent that's gotten off to a hot start.

"Microsoft is in a position to provide assistant services to its users as the main provider of software into millions of businesses," he said.

RBC Capital Markets analyst Rishi Jaluria added that Microsoft's latest move "is notable for what it signals about the evolving AI interface layer." He noted that the company is offering more coding and financial-operations tools.

-Hannah Pedone

data.title: The John Cooper School Director of Wellness Publishes New Book on Cultivating Well-Being in Education
data.description:
The John Cooper School Director of Wellness Publishes New Book on Cultivating Well-Being in Education

The John Cooper School Director of Wellness Publishes New Book on Cultivating Well-Being in Education

PR Newswire

THE WOODLANDS, Texas, Sept. 25, 2026

Dr. Juan-Diego Estrada's Beyond Thinking brings ideas shaped through Cooper's Wisdom in Action approach to educators and school communities worldwide

THE WOODLANDS, Texas, Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The John Cooper School is proud to celebrate Director of Wellness Dr. Juan-Diego Estrada on the publication of his new book, Beyond Thinking: Cultivating Awareness and Well-Being in Education, published by Bloomsbury Academic.

Drawing on more than two decades of experience bringing mindfulness and well-being practices to school communities, Dr. Estrada explores how educators can cultivate greater awareness, balance, and well-being in themselves and, in turn, in the students and communities they serve. The book combines neuroscience, mindfulness practices, and practical strategies designed to help educators and school leaders translate the principles of well-being into everyday practice.

Much of the work behind Beyond Thinking has been shaped through Dr. Estrada's experiences and the School's development of a systemic approach to well-being, articulated at Cooper as Wisdom in Action. At Cooper, Wisdom in Action reflects a commitment to educating the whole student by helping young people develop not only intellectually, but also socially, emotionally, and physically.

The book represents the latest chapter in work Dr. Estrada has advanced alongside Head of School Dr. Stephen Popp. Together, Dr. Estrada and Dr. Popp have presented Cooper's approach to well-being at national conferences and contributed to conversations about student wellness and whole-child education through leading education publications.

"Diego's work has helped us think deeply about what it means to educate and care for the whole student. Wisdom in Action reflects our belief that intellectual growth, personal well-being, and the development of character are deeply connected. It is incredibly meaningful to see ideas that have been cultivated and put into practice here at Cooper now reach educators and communities well beyond our campus through Beyond Thinking," said Dr. Stephen Popp.

In Beyond Thinking, Dr. Estrada examines the relationship between thinking, awareness, and well-being, offering educators practical ways to recognize unhelpful patterns, develop mindfulness skills, and create healthier learning environments. A central premise of the book is that meaningful change for students begins with the adults who teach, lead, and support them.

"Beyond Thinking grew out of years of working alongside students, educators, and colleagues at The John Cooper School and asking an important question: How do we help people not only succeed, but truly flourish? Wisdom in Action has given us the opportunity to put these ideas into practice and see how greater awareness can influence the way we learn, lead, and connect with one another. My hope is that this book gives educators and leaders practical tools they can use to create healthier, more intentional communities of their own," said Dr. Dr. Juan-Diego Estrada.

Published in 2026, the 200-page book has already received praise from leaders in the fields of education and youth well-being, including Marc Brackett, founding director of the Yale Center for Emotional Intelligence, and Alison Malmon, founder and Executive Director of Active Minds.

For The John Cooper School, the publication is both a celebration of Dr. Estrada's professional accomplishment and an opportunity to share ideas that have become an important part of the School's culture with educators beyond Cooper's campus.

Beyond Thinking: Cultivating Awareness and Well-Being in Education is available in print and digital formats through Bloomsbury Academic and major booksellers.

Learn more about Beyond Thinking:
Bloomsbury Academic – https://www.bloomsbury.com/us/beyond-thinking-9781475874600/
Amazon - https://www.amazon.com/Beyond-Thinking-Cultivating-Awareness-Well-Being/dp/147587460X 

The John Cooper School is an independent, non-sectarian, co-educational, college preparatory day school. The School's mission is to provide a challenging education in a caring environment to a diverse group of select students, enabling them to become critical and creative thinkers, effective communicators, responsible citizens and leaders, and lifelong learners.

data.title: Coca-Cola Taps Monster Executive as President of North American Unit
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton 




  Coca-Cola named Rob Gehring as president of its North America operating unit. 



  Gehring will start Dec. 1 and succeed John Murphy, who has led the unit on an interim basis since Aug. 1. Murphy remains president and chief financial officer. 



  Gehring, 59, most recently served as chief executive of Monster Energy's Americas business, which he started in February. 



  He began his career at Coca-Cola in 1992 before moving up to president of Coca-Cola's Walmart global team in 2011. In 2016, he joined Hershey, where he served as chief sales officer. 



  In 2018, Gehring was appointed as chief operating officer, and later chief executive, of Swire Coca-Cola, where he led bottling operations.
